title: Throughput economics A/B framework for dynamic batching and prefix-KV policies
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Goal: Build and run a statistically rigorous A/B framework that compares dynamic batching and prefix-KV caching policies against baseline configs, with an emphasis on economic metrics (cost per 1k tokens, tail latency penalties, and reliability). This ticket scopes the metric definitions, experiment traffic split mechanics, dashboards, and safe apply/rollback automation for low-risk production experiments. Motivation: previous experiments optimized token cost in isolation; teams requested a combined view that balances cost savings against 99th/95th latency tails and error surface.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible A/B experiment configuration that can be enabled per-customer-route with 0/25/50/100% traffic splits
Dashboard with primary economic metric (normalized cost-per-1k tokens), latency SLO overlays (p50/p95/p99), error rate, and request-level divergence histograms
Statistical test implementation that accounts for time-of-day traffic changes and produces decision guidance (win/lose/inconclusive) with confidence intervals
Automated safe-apply job that stages config to canary hosts and monitors smoke metrics for 10 minutes before progressing; automated rollback trigger on pre-defined guardrails
Playbook documented with runbook steps and links to PRs, Confluence spec, and responsible on-call owners
experiment_plan: Phase 0 (2 days): finalize metric definitions and dashboard wireframe; add synthetic workloads to traffic-replay simulator (ENG-28199)
Phase 1 (3 days): implement traffic-split flagging in routing layer (route metadata + experiment id); add sampling hooks for request attribution
Phase 2 (4 days): run 3-day A/B test (25/75 then 50/50) on non-critical internal customers using dynamic-batching profile + prefix-KV enabled vs baseline
Phase 3 (2 days): run statistical analysis job (SEE metrics) and produce recommendation; if >95% CI for cost reduction with <5% regression in p99, promote to broader canary
Phase 4 (ongoing): iterate on recommendations and integrate with Optimize suggestion engine
metrics: EffectiveThroughput: completed_tokens / GPU-second - helps measure batching efficiency
p99_latency_ms: 99th percentile latency (used as SLO guardrail)
ErrorRate: percent requests returning 5xx or model-fallback responses
TailPenaltyScore: weighted metric combining p99 latency and %requests over 500ms to capture user-perceived regressions
ConfigChurnEvents: counts of automatic rollbacks or manual reverts during the experiment
results_summary: Partial results from the first 24h canary (25% traffic) show a 12.4% reduction in NormalizedCostPer1kTokens, EffectiveThroughput improved by 18% during peak windows, but p99 latency increased by 9% on a small subset of long-context requests. ErrorRate remained stable. Statistical significance is marginal due to diurnal traffic variance; analysis job scheduled to run after 72h of mixed traffic.
rollout_plan: Canary 1: 25% internal routes for 24h with enhanced logging
Canary 2: 50% including low-risk customer routes for 48h if Canary 1 success criteria met
Broad canary: 75% for 72h with automated observability guardrails enabled
Full roll: 100% after two consecutive successful canaries or product sign-off
rollback_plan: Automated guardrail triggers: immediate rollback if p99 latency > baseline by 20% AND TailPenaltyScore increases by >10% for 10 minutes
If automated rollback triggers, route config reverted and incident ticket auto-created; on-call notified via PagerDuty
Manual rollback: engineers can trigger perf-revert pipeline that re-applies pinned baseline configs; requires follow-up hotfix PR for root-cause if repeated rollbacks occur

notes: Risks: long-context requests may amplify p99 regressions in certain kernels; mitigation includes per-route profile pinning and selective KV prefetching. Cost accounting alignment with finance is required to ensure applied infra_chargebacks are consistent across experiments. Coordinate with SRE on guardrail thresholds before broad canary.
